reasoning: mish is the Palestinian negator before a non-verb. heek has the long ee, written with kasra on the ي.
Form II active participle with the first vowel dropped. ط is emphatic T and the shadda doubles it. In Ramadan the same word means not fasting.
Urban Palestinian turns ذ into d in this inherited word, so the spelling is respelled كداب with shadda. MSA kadhdhaab is not how Ramallah says it.
Form II, shadda on غ, so the digraph gh is written twice. Used for switching on a device or starting an engine.
ق is a glottal stop and the final cluster takes a helping vowel, 'abil. After 'abil ma the verb has no b- prefix: truu7.
Past tense he-form. The same consonants also give the noun waja3, pain, but the given part of speech settles it as the verb.
The colloquial plural ends in -i, fawaaki, as the given spelling فواكي already shows, rather than MSA fawaakih.
In the construct the taa marbuta is pronounced t, so it is respelled as ت for the voice. Medial hamza and ق are both glottal stops.
Long oo in yoom, not uu. kam plus a singular noun is the ordinary way to say a few days.
ص is a sun letter, so the second article assimilates to iS-. A political formula of MSA shape that is genuinely said in Palestinian conversation and news talk.
yalla has shadda on ل. baay is the English loan, said with a long aa and a final y.
Palestinian raises both vowels of this verb class: li3ib, not MSA la3iba.
The nisba ending is -iyye with shadda on the ي. An MSA-shaped but normal shop-and-home term; a man's own underwear is often just lbaas.
Taa marbuta after ب is e. The adjective keeps the -iyye nisba with shadda. Ordinary Palestinian usage for a religious occasion.

From Si7i, which for weather means to clear. The b-imperfect he-form is biS7a, so the final ي is respelled as alif maqsura. I am unsure whether the intended reading is instead biSSa77a, hence low confidence.
zooj is understood and used in careful or polite speech, but the everyday Ramallah word for husband is jooz, with the consonants switched round.
Shadda on م. Specifically the sweet orange-fleshed melon or cantaloupe; watermelon is baTTiikh.
la plus ween, with the long ee written as kasra on the ي. Palestinian ween, not MSA ayna.
Form V with the dropped first vowel. The shadda doubles the digraph sh, giving shsh. Alif maqsura is romanized a.
Urban Palestinian shifts ث to t, as in ktiir and taalit, so the word is respelled خبيت. Educated speakers reading aloud may keep khabiith.
Form II bakkar with shadda on ك, literally to make early. م is a moon letter so the article stays il-.
Form III imperative saami7 loses its second vowel before the object suffix, giving saam7ni. ح is 7.
ق is a glottal stop in this everyday word. Taa marbuta after ع is a.
Said shaa7ne with the middle vowel dropped and taa marbuta as e. In casual Ramallah speech loori or trak is at least as common for a lorry.
براغي is the broken plural of burghi, so the English singular does not match the Arabic.
